artboards.title: A block is what you place

annotations.text:
THE SCREEN. A material shows the patch it actually draws — its archetype's slots, assembled — beside the raw slots, and a Meets list of everything it can touch.

Picking a pairing swaps the preview for that transition. Same screen, same shape; one material became two and the empty half of each slot filled in. The list is a way of looking, not a form.

An archetype owns a vocabulary of slots — floor's are the sixteen corner masks, wall's are named parts including its seams, ramp's are parts at a root-2 aspect.

A material fills that vocabulary with its own art. A transition fills the SAME vocabulary with two to four materials meeting. So transitions live in every archetype.

OPEN: how much resolution a non-corner slot needs. A wall's face slot is one tile, so stone becoming wood along a run is abrupt; a small left/right mask would let it feather.

Also: a transition's archetype belongs to the transition, not its materials, so one pairing may have a floor block and a wall strip.

The boards below are kept in the order they were drawn, with their supersessions noted, so the reasoning stays legible. Shapes is right that 16 beats 47; Seams is right that a seam cannot be a corner tag; both predate archetypes owning their own vocabularies.
